newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland Bank supervisors retain markka influence.
newsitem.headline: Finland Bank supervisors retain markka influence.

text.p: The Bank of Finland's board of parliamentary supervisors will retain its role in decisions concerning the exchange rate of the markka, an official at parliament's constitutional committee said on Thursday.

In its ruling on a government proposal to reform central bank legislation, the committee said that "one narrow segment" of the reform package needed special treatment in parliament to become law, committee secretary Jarmo Vuorinen told Reuters by telephone.
The segment he referred to is the Money Act, which governs the procedure for changes in the markka exchange rate.

The government proposed that decisions about the markka exchange rate should be transferred to the central bank's board of management, stripping the board of parliamentary supervisors of its key role.

The constitutional committee found that such a transfer would alter the decision-making powers in such a fundamental way that parliamentary approval by a two-thirds majority is required, Vuorinen said.
"And first it would need a five-sixths majority to be declared urgent," he added.
